correctness.rationale: The exact dyadic plateau formula follows by induction. For every \(y\in[0,1]\), the identity \(2\Phi(Ty)-\Phi(y)-y=\tfrac45(1-2y)\) on \([0,1/2]\) and zero on \([1/2,1]\), with \(\Phi(y)=4/5-y/5\), gives a telescoping weighted-orbit bound. An independent affine endpoint inequality covers every partial plateau, proving \(\sum_{n<N}u_n\le4N/5+x/5\) for all initial points and times. The legal right-inverse orbit \(z_{-j}=\frac23(1-(-1/2)^j)\) has discounted sum \(4/5\). Dense orbits shadow finite pieces of that backward orbit and of the fixed zero orbit at arbitrarily late times, giving limsup \(4/5\) and liminf \(0\) at complete-block indices. The one-step average change is at most \(1/(N+1)\), so all intermediate limits occur. The fair-Bernoulli coding of the full tent map proves almost-everywhere density and ordinary ergodic mean \(1/2\). The standalone program passed 71,844 exact rational checks, supplementary to this proof.

value.rationale: Physical-time averaging is a natural observable for a delayed chaotic map with exponentially growing stasis. While ordinary tent-map iterates have almost-sure mean \(1/2\), the held orbit has accumulation interval \([0,4/5]\) for almost every initial point. The nontrivial \(4/5\) endpoint is optimized by an explicit legal backward history. The result determines the whole physically timed statistical response of a natural expanding-map example, not merely the known plateau identity.
